previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of systolic heart failure (EF 20%), ischemic cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and obstructive sleep apnea, was readmitted one week after discharge for worsening dyspnea and leg swelling. He had gained weight and was found to have increased interstitial edema on chest X-ray and elevated BNP. He was treated with IV furosemide and transitioned to oral torsemide, with improvement in symptoms and weight. Fluid and sodium restrictions were reinforced, and his medications were optimized. His ICD was checked and functioning normally. He was discharged with plans to follow up with cardiology and primary care for ongoing management of heart failure, diabetes, and sleep apnea.
